title: Erythromycin fermentation process dataset
question: How do chemical-potency trajectories vary across independent fermentation batches and recorded cultivation time?
publisher: Yan, Xuefeng (East China University of Science and Technology); Sun, Yifei (East China University of Science and Technology)
measurement_dates: Description says 2022; retained rows span December 26, 2021 to November 14, 2022 in file order. Preserve mismatch.
variables_and_units: hourly process variables and fermentation response
independent_units: complete fermentation batches, chronological batch blocks
validation_design: complete fermentation batches, chronological batch blocks Verify identifiers before allocating groups; the partition is not executed or frozen by this acquisition.
author_preprocessing: Historical industrial exports: 50,536 rows, 406 batches, and hx as the chemical-potency target selected by the source loader. Several process abbreviations and physical units are not defined in the deposit; no meanings are guessed.
prior_analysis_and_limits: Keep all samples of each batch together. Restrict currently defensible modeling to documented target/time/batch structure and explicitly source-unit or dimensionless response; physical laws involving unmapped process variables need an additional verified dictionary. The description claims an average of 154 samples per batch, while the retained 50,536 rows imply about 124.5; preserve this inconsistency.
missingness: Native blanks, sentinels, absent records and source quality flags are preserved. No imputation performed by the curator. Exact missingness semantics come from source dictionaries/headers; no universal missing-value rule is imposed.
calibration: Use the retained source calibration files/standards and instrument metadata where provided. Absence of an explicit calibration record is not replaced by an assumed calibration.

eligibility.novelty: no unseen-law guarantee; independent adjudication required

exposure: Open source-aware; source literature and supplied analyses accessible
unit_interpretation: Use exact source field/sheet/channel labels and units in source_evidence and per-file reports; unknown units remain unresolved, not inferred from a variable name.
